newsitem.title: JAPAN: TSE says Big Bang panel report positive for market.
newsitem.headline: TSE says Big Bang panel report positive for market.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) gave high marks to a panel's proposals for Japan's "Big Bang" reforms on Friday, saying the measures should be positive for the securities market as a whole.

"We highly appreciate the recommendations, which tackled difficult issues without making any exceptions and also covered basic legal and taxation systems," TSE chairman Mitsuhide Yamaguchi said in a statement.

"The specific proposals include some items which will bring some pain, but as a whole they are positive, or we should make it positive, for individual market participants as well as the market as a whole."
The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA), meanwhile, said in a statement that it welcomed the panel's recommendations as they paved the way for securities market reform.
The JSDA said that it would strive to carry out the proposed reforms in the securities market to create a market equal to its foreign counterparts towards the 21th century.

Earlier, the Securities and Exchange Council, a panel to the finance minister, urged a two-phase liberalisation of stock brokerage commissions, to be completed by the end of 1999, and the opening up of the securities business to new participants. It also urged Japan to break down barriers between banks and brokers by March 2000.
